claims.head: Don’t buy Oettinger’s record against the Sabres
claims.body: Oettinger has been a wall against the Sabres since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Oettinger isn’t that wall tonight.

story.head: The Stars’ edge in the penalty kill
paras: The Stars won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-0 in Buffalo on Oct 8. The Stars (10-6-2) lost 8-3 to Winnipeg on Thursday, and the Sabres are winless in three (0-2-1). Going in, the Sabres are sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 18th in the NHL) and the Stars fourth in the Central (tied for 14th).
This season, the Sabres have been outscored 67-55, but only 40-38 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 21-11.

The Sabres get their defensemen shooting (5th) and rarely get pinned in their own end (5th), but don't block many shots (30th). On the other side, the Stars play slow, tight games (lowest) and have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st). They also block more shots than anyone (1st), and the Sabres’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot. The Stars have the edge over the Sabres on the penalty kill.

Tage Thompson (12 G / 9 A / 21 P in 19 GP) leads the Sabres in scoring, with four goals in six games against Dallas since 2023-24. Jack Quinn (9 G / 10 A / 19 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Stars, Mikko Rantanen (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 18 GP) leads the way in scoring. Jason Robertson (9 G / 11 A / 20 P in 18 GP) isn’t far behind, with seven points in his last five games.

Jake Oettinger (9-4-1 / .895 SV% in 14 GS) will likely start for Dallas. Buffalo has two options in net: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (5-4-3 / .867 SV% in 11 GS) and Colten Ellis (3-3-0 / .873 SV% in 7 GS). Luukkonen has started five of their last ten games, including the last one on Wednesday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net. Oettinger has a .937 save percentage in five starts against the Sabres, well above his usual .903. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
